messages.content: Our teacher wants us to give a two-minute talk on any topic next week. I have no idea what to pick.
Pick something you already know well and enjoy, so you won't need much research. A hobby, a place you love or a skill you learned can all work. What do you like doing on weekends?
I like flying kites with my uncle on the terrace.
That could make a lovely talk. You could explain how a kite is made, how you choose a windy day, and share one funny moment with your uncle. Three short parts fit nicely into two minutes.
What if I forget my lines in front of everyone?

Don't learn it word for word. Write the three parts on a small card, one line each, and glance at it when you need to. Practise aloud at home two or three times, and time yourself so you know it fits.
My grandfather is moving in with us next week, and I have to share my room with him for a while.
That is a big change, and it is fair to have mixed feelings about it. Sharing a room takes some adjusting for both of you. How do you feel about it so far?
I love him, but I'm worried I won't get any privacy. I also study late.
Both worries make sense. You could ask your parents about a small study corner elsewhere for late evenings, like the dining table. A curtain or a bookshelf can also divide the room a little.
Should I say something to him too?

Yes, kindly and early. Ask him what he needs, like when he sleeps and wakes, and tell him your study hours. When you both know each other's routine, small problems are easier to solve before they grow.
Priya and Neha both invited me to their birthday parties, and they're on the same evening.
That is a tricky spot, since you probably don't want to hurt either friend. Are the parties at the same time, or is one earlier than the other?
Priya's starts at five and Neha's at seven. They live about twenty minutes apart.

Then you may be able to attend both. You could spend about an hour and a half at Priya's, leave around half past six, and reach Neha's a little before seven. Tell both of them your plan in advance so nobody is surprised when you leave or arrive.
My mom said she can drop me.
Good, that makes it easy. Confirm the timings with your mom today, and keep both gifts ready and labelled so you don't mix them up on the way.
I want to pack a healthier tiffin for myself, but I hate boring food.
Healthy does not have to mean boring. Colour and crunch make a big difference. What do you usually take now?
Mostly bread and jam, or chips if I'm in a hurry.

You could swap one thing at a time. Try a vegetable sandwich with a little chutney, or a roll made from last night's roti and sabzi. Add a fruit you like, such as a banana or a few grapes, for something sweet.
The roll idea is good. My mornings are rushed though.
Then fill the roll at night and keep it in the fridge. In the morning, you only need to pack it. A ready box takes less than a minute, which is faster than buying chips.
My family is taking an overnight train to Chennai, and I've never slept on a train before.
It can be a fun experience. The gentle rocking helps many people fall asleep. Do you know if you have an upper, middle or lower berth?
I think I have the upper berth.

The upper berth is quite private, and nobody needs it during the day, so you can lie down whenever you like. Keep a small bag with water, a torch and a light shawl up there with you, since trains can get cold at night.
What about my shoes and the big suitcase?
Put the suitcase under the lower seat, and lock it to the chain there if you have a lock. Put your shoes under the seat too, toes pointing in, so nobody trips over them in the dark.
My manager asked me to lead the team meeting tomorrow because she is on leave.
That shows she trusts you. Leading one meeting is a good chance to practise. Do you know what needs to be covered?
She sent me a short list of four points.

Then the meeting already has a shape. Start by thanking everyone and saying how long it will take. Go through the four points in order, give each a few minutes, and note any decisions. End by reading out who will do what.
What if two people start arguing?
Stay calm and neutral. You can say, "Both points are useful. Let's note them and let our manager decide when she's back." That keeps the meeting moving without taking sides.
We're celebrating Onam at my friend's house this year, and I don't know much about it.
Onam is a harvest festival celebrated mainly in Kerala. Families make flower carpets called pookalam and share a big vegetarian feast called the sadya. Are you joining for the meal?
Yes, the sadya. Is there anything I should know?

The sadya is usually served on a banana leaf, and many people eat with their right hand. There will be many small dishes, so take a little of each at first. Watch your friend's family and follow their lead.
Should I take something along?
A small box of sweets or some flowers would be a kind gesture. The flowers might even end up in the pookalam if they are making one.
I want to start running in the mornings but I get tired after five minutes.
That is very normal at the start. Most new runners go too fast. Have you tried mixing running with walking?
No, I just run until I can't anymore.
Try this instead: run for one minute, then walk for two, and repeat it six or seven times. Run slowly enough that you could still talk. Over a few weeks, run a little longer and walk a little less.
How often should I go?
Three mornings a week is a good start, with a rest day in between. Rest days give your legs time to recover. Tiredness is normal, but if something actually hurts, stop and take a break.
There's a bird building a nest on our window ledge.
How lovely. Do you know what kind of bird it is?
I think it's a pigeon. My dad wants to remove it.
Pigeons often nest on ledges because they feel safe there. If the nest has no eggs yet, now is the easiest time to decide. Once there are eggs or chicks, moving the nest can harm them.
Can we keep it until the babies leave?
You could ask your dad about that. Pigeon chicks usually leave the nest about a month after hatching. Keeping that window shut and not touching the nest will help both your family and the birds.
My book club picked a really long novel and I'm only on chapter three.
Long novels can feel slow at first, especially while the characters are being introduced. When is the club meeting?
In two weeks. The book has forty chapters.
That means about three chapters a day. If you read for half an hour before bed, you can probably keep up. Some days you will read more, which gives you a cushion.
And if I still don't finish?
Go anyway. You can share what you thought of the part you read, and the discussion may even make you want to finish it. Nobody in a book club should feel left out for being behind.
I keep comparing myself to my older brother. He's good at everything.
That can be tiring, especially when others compare you too. Is there something people say that makes you feel this way?
Relatives always ask why my marks aren't like his.
That hurts, and it is not a fair comparison. You are different people, with different strengths and different years. Your brother's marks say nothing about your worth.
But I'm not really good at anything.

It may feel that way right now, but strengths are not only marks. Being kind, being funny or being good with your hands all count. Think about what friends come to you for. That is often a clue to what you are good at.
My cat has started scratching the new sofa.
Cats scratch to keep their claws healthy and to mark their space, so she is not being naughty. Does she have a scratching post?
No. Do we really need one?
Yes, it gives her a better place to scratch. Put it right next to the sofa, since that is the spot she has chosen. Rub a little catnip on it, or play with a string near it, so she notices it.
Should we cover the sofa till then?
That is a good idea. A thick blanket over the scratched corner makes it less fun for her. Once she uses the post regularly, you can slowly move it to where you want it.
I bought a sketchbook a month ago and haven't drawn a single thing.
A blank sketchbook can feel strangely scary. Many people worry about spoiling the first page. Does that sound familiar?
Yes! I want every page to look good.

Then try this: on the first page, draw something messy on purpose, like scribbles or a cup drawn with your eyes closed. Once the first page is "ruined," the rest feels free. The sketchbook is for practice, not for showing off.
What should I draw after that?
Draw small things around you, like your shoes, a key or a mug. Give each one five minutes. Simple objects teach shape and shading, and you can finish them in one sitting.
I'm moving into my first rented flat with two friends.
Congratulations, that is an exciting step. Living with friends is fun, but it helps to agree on a few things early. Have you talked about chores yet?
Not really. We just assumed it will work out.

It often works out better with a simple plan. Make a chart for cooking, washing up and cleaning the bathroom, and rotate it every week. Also agree on how you will split shared costs like groceries and electricity.
What if one of them doesn't do their part?
Bring it up early, calmly and in private. Talk about the task, not the person: "The dishes were left for two days. Can we sort it out?" Small issues are easier to fix than a pile of resentment.
It's so hot this week that I can't sleep at night.
Heat makes sleep very hard. Is your room facing the afternoon sun?
Yes, the west side. It stays warm till midnight.
Keep the curtains closed in the afternoon to block the sun, and open the windows after sunset when the air outside cools. A damp cloth hung near the window can also cool the air a little.
Anything else that helps?
A cool bath before bed, light cotton clothes and cotton sheets all help. Some families sleep on a mat on the floor in summer, since it is often cooler than the bed.
My school choir has a concert next month and I got a small solo.
Congratulations! A solo, even a small one, means the teacher trusts your voice. How do you feel about it?
Excited but scared. My voice shakes when I'm nervous.

That is common, even for experienced singers. Slow breathing helps. Before your part, breathe in for four counts and out for six. Practising the solo many times also helps, because your body learns it and needs less effort on the day.
Should I practise in front of people first?
Yes, start small. Sing it for your family, then for a friend or two. Each small audience makes the real one feel less strange.
My grandmother just got her first smartphone and keeps calling me for help.
It's sweet that she turns to you. Learning a new phone at any age takes patience. What does she find hardest?
Mostly video calls. She can never find the button.
You could make her a simple guide on paper. Write three steps in big letters, maybe with small drawings of each button. Keep it next to her phone.
She also says the text is too small.
Most phones let you make the text and icons bigger in the settings. Do it for her once, and show her the change. Bigger text often makes everything else feel easier too.
I got into two colleges and I have to choose by Friday.
Congratulations on getting into both. That is a good problem to have. What are the main differences between them?
One is in my city and cheaper. The other is far away but has a better course.
Those are both real reasons. Try listing what matters most to you: the course, the cost, being near family, or living on your own. Rank them, then see which college fits your top two.
The course matters most, but I'm scared of living alone.

Many first-year students feel that fear, and for most it fades within a few months. You could ask the far college about hostels and student groups. Talking to a current student there may also make it feel less unknown.
I need new shoes for school but I can't decide between two pairs.
What are the two pairs like?
One looks really cool but pinches a little. The other is plain but comfortable.
Shoes that pinch in the shop usually feel worse after a full day of walking. Since you will wear them to school every day, comfort matters a lot.
But the cool ones are what everyone is wearing.
That is understandable. You could take the comfortable pair for school and save up for the stylish ones later for outings. Your feet will thank you on long school days.
Our colony is planning a cleanliness drive this Sunday and I want to help.
That is a kind thing to do. What kind of help do they need?
They asked for volunteers to collect plastic from the park.
Then wear clothes you don't mind getting dirty, closed shoes and gloves. Carry a water bottle and a cap if it is sunny. Keep separate bags for plastic and other waste so it can be sorted easily.
Can I bring my younger cousin? She's eight.
Yes, children often enjoy it. Give her a simple job, like holding the bag or picking up wrappers on the grass. Keep her away from glass or sharp things, and make sure she wears gloves too.
Our science project partner hasn't done any of his part, and the project is due Monday.
That is stressful, especially so close to the deadline. Have you talked to him about it yet?
I messaged him twice. He just says "I'll do it."
Try making it specific. Instead of asking in general, say, "Can you send me the chart by Saturday noon?" A clear task and a clear time are harder to ignore.
And if he still doesn't send it?
Then tell your teacher before Monday, calmly and honestly. Show what you have done. Teachers usually prefer hearing early to finding out on the deadline.
My parents are celebrating their twenty-fifth anniversary next month.
That's a wonderful milestone. Are you planning something for them?
Yes, with my sister. We want it to be a surprise.
A surprise can be lovely. You could collect old photos from relatives and make a small album, or invite close family for dinner. What do your parents enjoy most?
They love old songs and going to the beach.

Then you could combine both. Plan an evening walk on the beach, followed by dinner at home with their favourite songs playing. Ask each relative to write one short memory of them, and read a few aloud.
A new girl joined our class and she sits alone at lunch.
It is kind that you noticed. Starting at a new school can be lonely. Do you know her name?
Her name is Ayesha. I don't really know what to say to her.
Something simple works well. You could say, "Hi Ayesha, do you want to sit with us?" or ask where she studied before. You don't need a perfect line, just a friendly one.
What if my friends don't like it?
Most people warm up quickly when someone new is friendly. Introduce her to them by name. If one of them is cold to her, that says more about them than about you or Ayesha.
I tried making chapatis for the first time and they came out hard.
First chapatis are often hard, so don't worry. How did you make the dough?
I just mixed flour and water until it held together.
The dough may have been too stiff. It should feel soft and smooth. Knead it for a few minutes, then cover it and let it rest for about twenty minutes before rolling.
My mom said I cooked them too long too.
That can dry them out. Cook each side on a hot tawa only until small brown spots appear. Then it is done. You can keep them soft by stacking them in a box lined with a cloth.
We're going to visit Jaipur for three days during the winter break.
Jaipur is a good choice for winter, as the days are pleasant. Have you made a plan yet?
Not really. My parents want forts, my sister wants shopping.
Then you could split each day. Visit a fort in the morning, when it is cooler and less crowded, and spend the evening in a market. That way everyone gets something they like.
Which fort should we see first?
Many visitors start with Amber Fort, since it is large and needs the most time. Go early in the morning. On the other days you can see the smaller sights in the city.
I've been working from home for a month and I feel like I never stop.
That is a common problem with working from home. Without a commute, work can spill into the whole day. Do you have a fixed start and finish time?
I start at nine, but I keep checking messages till late.
Try setting a clear end time, maybe half past six, and turn off work notifications after that. Closing your laptop and putting it away can also signal that the day is over.
My boss sometimes messages at night though.
You could ask your boss directly what is urgent and what can wait till morning. Most managers are fine with next-day replies for normal tasks. Once you know, you can relax more in the evenings.
This is my first Christmas away from home. I'm living in a hostel.
Holidays can feel lonely when you are far from family. Are any other students staying in the hostel over the break?
A few, mostly from other states.
You could invite them for a small get-together. Each person could bring a snack from their home region and share one tradition. It can turn a lonely day into a warm one.
I'd also like to call my family that morning.
That's a good idea. Fix a time with them in advance so everyone is there. Seeing their faces on a call, then spending the evening with new friends, can make the day feel full.
I want to learn swimming but I'm twenty and I feel embarrassed.
Lots of adults learn to swim, so you would not be the only one. Many pools have adult beginner classes. Have you looked for one near you?
There's a pool near my office. They have classes at seven in the morning.
Early classes are usually quieter, which may help you feel less shy. Instructors who teach adults are used to nervous beginners.
What should I take on the first day?
A swimsuit, a towel, a cap and goggles are the basics. Take a change of clothes and a small bag for wet things. Reach a few minutes early so you can ask the instructor any questions.
We're going camping near a lake this weekend. It's my first time.
How exciting! Camping by a lake can be very peaceful. Will you be staying in tents?
Yes, with my scout group.
Then pack light but warm. Nights near water can be colder than you expect. Take a torch, a water bottle, a jacket and a spare set of clothes in a plastic bag so they stay dry.
What if I see snakes?

Most snakes avoid people and move away if left alone. Keep your distance, never try to touch or catch one, and tell your scout leader. Wearing closed shoes and using a torch at night also helps you see where you step.
I'm writing a short story for a competition but I'm stuck halfway.
Getting stuck in the middle is very common. What happens in your story so far?
A boy finds an old key in his grandmother's house, but I don't know what it opens.
That is a strong start. Ask yourself what the boy wants most. The key could open something linked to that wish, like a box of letters from a parent or a room nobody talks about.
I like the box of letters idea.
Then you have a direction. The letters could show him something new about his family. Let him find one surprising detail, and build the ending around how that changes him.
I auditioned for the lead in our school play and got a tiny role instead.
That is disappointing, especially if you worked hard for it. How are you feeling about it?
Embarrassed. My friend got the lead and everyone keeps congratulating her.
It is hard to be happy for a friend while you are hurting, and both feelings can exist together. You don't have to pretend you are fine, but you can still congratulate her.
Is a small role even worth doing?

Yes. Small roles teach you how a show runs, and directors notice people who do them well. Use rehearsals to learn from the lead role too. Next time, you will go into the audition with more experience.
My parents finally agreed to get a fish tank.
That is exciting. Fish can be calming to watch. Have you decided what fish you want?
I want lots of colourful ones.
It helps to start with a few hardy fish, since some colourful types need special care. Ask at the shop which ones are good for beginners and which can live together.
When can I put them in?
Set up the tank with water, the filter and plants first, and let it run for a while before adding fish. The shop can tell you how long. Then add only a few fish at a time, so the water stays clean.
I've started learning to knit from my aunt, and my rows keep getting uneven.
Uneven rows are normal when you are learning. Your hands are still finding the right tension. Do the stitches get tighter or looser as you go?
Tighter. By the end of the row, the needle barely fits.
That usually means you are pulling the yarn too hard, often from nerves. Try to relax your grip and slide each stitch onto the thick part of the needle, not the tip.
Should I start again?
You don't need to. Keep this piece as a practice square and see how your rows improve. Comparing the first rows with the last ones later will show you how far you have come.
Our kitchen sink keeps getting blocked.
That is annoying. Blocks usually come from food bits or grease going down the drain. Do you have a strainer in the sink?
No, we just rinse plates straight into it.
A simple mesh strainer catches most food bits. Scrape plates into the bin before washing, and never pour leftover oil down the drain, since it hardens in the pipe.
What about the block that's there now?
Pouring hot water slowly down the drain can sometimes loosen grease. If the water still won't go down, it is better to call a plumber than to keep trying strong chemicals.
The forecast says a cyclone might reach our coast this week.
That sounds worrying. The most important thing is to follow local news and official warnings. Do you live close to the sea?
About two kilometres away. My parents seem quite relaxed about it.
It still helps to prepare early. Keep torches, spare batteries, drinking water and some dry food ready. Charge phones and power banks, and keep important papers in a waterproof bag.
What if they tell us to leave?
Then leave when officials say so, and don't wait. Find out where the nearest shelter is, and decide in advance where your family will meet if you get separated.
My neighbour plays the sitar every evening and I'd love to learn.
What a lucky thing to hear every day. Have you ever spoken to your neighbour about it?
Just a hello. I'm not sure if it's okay to ask.
Many musicians are happy when someone shows real interest. You could praise the playing and ask how your neighbour started. That opens the topic gently without asking for lessons straight away.
And if he offers to teach me?
Then ask about timings and whether he takes fees, so things are clear from the start. Be on time, and practise between lessons. Teachers enjoy students who show steady effort.
My laptop has become really slow lately.
That is frustrating. Do you know how full the storage is?
It says only a small amount of space is left.
A nearly full drive can slow a computer down. Start by deleting large files you don't need, like old videos and downloads. Move photos to an external drive if you want to keep them.
I also have lots of programs that start when I switch it on.
Those can slow down startup. Look in the settings for startup apps and turn off the ones you don't need right away. Restart the laptop afterwards to see if it helped.
My college has a fest next month and I want to join the organising team.
That is a great way to meet people and learn new skills. Do you know which team you want to be on?
Maybe decoration or hospitality. I'm not sure.
Think about what you enjoy. Decoration suits you if you like making things with your hands. Hospitality suits you if you like talking to people and solving small problems quickly.
I like talking to people more.
Then hospitality sounds like your fit. When you sign up, mention a time you looked after guests or handled a crowd, even at a family event. It shows you already have some experience.
I'm buying my first winter jacket on my own this weekend.
That's a nice step. Do you know how cold it gets where you live?
Not very cold, maybe ten degrees at night.
Then you don't need a heavy jacket. A light padded one or a fleece would be enough. Check that you can move your arms easily and that the zip runs smoothly.
Should I buy one size bigger?
A little room is good, so you can wear a sweater underneath. Try it on over a thick top in the shop. If the sleeves cover your hands, it is too big.
The old library in our area might close because hardly anyone visits.
That would be a loss for the neighbourhood. Do you use it yourself?
I used to, as a kid. I'd like to help keep it open.
You could start by asking the librarian what would help most. Some libraries run reading clubs, homework hours or story time for children, which bring people in.
I could run a story hour for little kids on Saturdays.
That is a lovely idea. Pick short picture books, keep each session to about forty-five minutes, and put up notices in the building and nearby shops. Even a few regular families can make a difference.
I'm moving up to class nine and everyone says it's much harder.
Class nine does bring more depth, but many students manage it well with steady habits. What worries you most?
Science. There's physics, chemistry and biology all together.
Treat them as three short subjects, not one big one. Spend a little time on each every week, rather than cramming one at a time. Keep a separate notebook or section for each.
My friends say tuition is a must.
Not always. Many students do well by paying attention in class and asking teachers when they get stuck. Try the first few weeks on your own, and decide later if you need extra help.
My little brother is scared of the dark and wakes me up every night.
That must be tiring for you. Fear of the dark is very common in young children. How old is he?
He's six. He comes to my bed at two in the morning.
You could suggest a small night light in his room. Reading a calm story with him at bedtime can also help him feel safe before he sleeps.
My parents said I should be patient.
Patience will help, but you can also tell them what you need, since you need sleep too. Maybe they can take turns comforting him at night. That way it is not all on you.
My friend Rohan borrowed my bicycle two weeks ago and hasn't returned it.
That is frustrating, especially if you need it. Has he said anything about it?
No. I don't want to sound rude by asking.
Asking for your own things back is not rude. You could say, "Hey Rohan, I need my bicycle this weekend. Can you bring it on Friday?" A clear day makes it simple.
What if it's damaged?
Then talk about it calmly when you see it. He may not even know it got damaged. Ask him to help fix it, since it happened while he had it.
My roommate and I want to cook more and order less.
That's a good plan, and cooking together can be fun. How often do you order food now?
Almost every night.
Then don't try to cook every day at once. Start with three nights a week. Pick easy meals like khichdi, egg curry or pasta, and shop for those three meals on the weekend.
We always run out of time on weeknights.
Do some prep on Sunday. Chop onions, wash vegetables and boil a few eggs, then store them in boxes in the fridge. On weeknights, dinner then takes twenty minutes instead of an hour.
I'm flying alone for the first time to visit my aunt in Pune.
That is a big step. Do you know your flight time?
Yes, it's at six in the morning. I'm seventeen, by the way.
Then plan to reach the airport about two hours early, so around four. Keep your ID and ticket in one easy pocket. Pack your bag the night before, and check the rules for liquids in hand luggage.
What if I get lost inside the airport?

Airports have lots of signs and staff. Look for the screens showing your flight number and gate. If you are unsure, ask at the airline counter or any staff member. Text your aunt once you board and again when you land.
I have my first performance review next week and I don't know what to expect.
It's normal to feel unsure the first time. A review is usually a talk about what went well, what can improve and your goals. Have you been given a form to fill in?
Yes, they asked me to list my achievements.
Then think back over the year and write down specific things you did, with results if possible. For example, "Finished the report two days early" is better than "Worked hard."
What if they criticise me?
Listen calmly and take notes. Ask for an example if a point is unclear, and ask how you can improve. Treating feedback as information, not as an attack, usually makes the meeting go better.
We're making our own Ganesh idol from clay this year.
That's a wonderful idea. A clay idol is also kinder to rivers and lakes. Have you worked with clay before?
Only in school, a long time ago.
Start with simple shapes. Make the body from one large ball, then add the head, ears and trunk as smaller pieces. Keep a bowl of water nearby to smooth the joins.
Can we paint it?
Yes, but natural colours like turmeric are a better choice if you plan to immerse it in water. Let the clay dry fully for a few days before painting.
Our football team keeps losing in the last ten minutes of matches.
That often means players are getting tired near the end. Do you train for stamina, or mostly skills?
Mostly skills. We play small matches in practice.
Add some running to training, like short sprints with rest in between. Matches need bursts of speed again and again, and sprints build that.
What else can we do during the match?
Use your substitutes wisely, and bring fresh legs on before players are completely tired. Keep talking on the field, especially near the end, so nobody drifts out of position.
I saw fireflies in my grandparents' village last night. I'd never seen them before.
That must have been magical. Fireflies are harder to see in cities because of the bright lights. Where did you see them?
In the bushes near the paddy fields. Why do they glow?
Fireflies make light inside their bodies through a chemical reaction. They use the flashes to signal to each other, a bit like a code.
Can I catch one in a jar to show my friends?
It is better to let them be. Fireflies can get stressed or die in a jar. You could take your friends to see them one evening, or describe what you saw. Some sights are best left where they are.
My little sister is five and she doesn't like books at all.
Many young children warm up to books slowly. What does she like doing most?
She loves animals and drawing.
Then try picture books about animals, with big colourful pictures and only a few words on each page. Let her choose the books herself at the library.
She gets bored when I read to her.

Try making it lively. Use funny voices for the animals and ask her what she thinks will happen next. After reading, she could draw her favourite part. That links the story to something she already loves.
